PlayerKarteaSessionDetail

class PlayerKarteaSessionDetail(id, session, event_date, event_time, phase, level, player_position, event_position, event_type)[source]

Bases: ReflexiveModel

Detailed model for Kartea player session event data.

Each instance is one event (collision, lane change, menu choice, …) written as a row of the player’s session detail CSV.

Attributes:
idint

Unique identifier for the event.

sessionPlayerKarteaSession

The session in which the event happened.

event_datestr

Event date, ISO 8601 “%Y-%m-%d” (formerly the date_time column).

event_timestr

Event time, ISO 8601 “%H:%M:%S” (local time).

phaseint

Game phase when the event happened.

levelint

Game level when the event happened.

player_positionint

Lane of the player when the event happened.

event_positionint

Lane related to the event: the object’s lane for collisions/avoidances, the previous lane for lane changes; 0 when the event has no position.

event_typeEventType | str

Type of the event. Holds an EventType when recorded by the game and the plain pt_BR text when read from the CSV.

EventTypetype[Enum], class attribute

Types of events recorded in a session detail.

_DISPLAY_TEXTSClassVar[dict[EventType, str]], class attribute

pt_BR display text of each EventType, marked for translation; equal to the value stored in the CSV.

PROPERTIESClassVar[list[str]], class attribute

Field names of the class, filled by initialize_reflexive.

DATA_PROPERTIESClassVar[list], class attribute

Default value of each init field (dataclasses.MISSING when the field has none), filled by initialize_reflexive.

REF_PROPERTIEStuple[str, …], class attribute

Fields written as the referenced object’s id by get_data: ("session",).

Notes

Internationalization (i18n): the EventType values are what the CSV stores. The text shown to the user comes from _DISPLAY_TEXTS, whose entries are marked with QT_TRANSLATE_NOOP in the "PlayerKarteaSessionDetail" context so that pyside6-lupdate extracts them (it only extracts string literals, so the texts are repeated there); the translation happens at display time through EventType.display_name (QCoreApplication.translate). Each display text is kept equal to its EventType value. Add an entry to _DISPLAY_TEXTS with the same text for every new event.

Changing a value changes what new rows store: rows already in the CSV keep the old text and are read back as plain text. E.g. “Controle Jogo: Avanca Nível” and “Controle Jogador: Jogar” are now “Controle do Jogo: Avança Nível” and “Controle do Jogador: Jogar”.

Examples

>>> from types import SimpleNamespace
>>> EventType = PlayerKarteaSessionDetail.EventType
>>> detail = PlayerKarteaSessionDetail(
...     id=1,
...     session=SimpleNamespace(id=5),
...     event_date="2025-09-17",
...     event_time="10:00:00",
...     phase=1,
...     level=2,
...     player_position=2,
...     event_position=1,
...     event_type=EventType.CHANGED_LANE,
... )
>>> data = detail.get_data()[0]
>>> data["session"], data["event_type"]
(5, 'Trocou de Pista')
class EventType(value)[source]

Bases: str, Enum

Types of events recorded in a session detail.

Groups of members:

  • COLLIDED_*/AVOIDED_*: collisions with and avoidances of targets and obstacles.

  • CREATED_*: objects created on the track.

  • CHANGED_LANE, LEFT_GAME_AREA: player movement.

  • GAME_CONTROL_*: level progression decided by the game.

  • UFE_CONTROL_*: HUD, sound, pause, feet marker and feet click toggles, and the professional’s choices in the pause and end-of-level menus (mouse or keyboard).

  • PLAYER_CONTROL_*: the same menu choices made by the player with the feet (feet click).

Notes

The enum mixes in str, so each value is the pt_BR text written to the CSV; keep the matching entry of _DISPLAY_TEXTS with the same text. Use display_name to show the event in the active Qt language.

property display_name: str

Event name translated into the active Qt language.

Notes

Looks up the pt_BR display text in PlayerKarteaSessionDetail._DISPLAY_TEXTS (falling back to the stored value) and translates it at runtime with QCoreApplication.translate in the "PlayerKarteaSessionDetail" context (i18n); Qt returns the pt_BR text when there is no translation.
